standard_prerequisites.name: Self centralizing subfields
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the image of the field in the opposite algebra is its own centralizer, which identifies the tensor product with the centralizer of the ground field inside an endomorphism algebra.

standard_prerequisites.name: The commutant and the Brauer group
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the class of the commutant is the negative of the class of the algebra in the Brauer group, which gives similarity of the two algebras.

standard_prerequisites.name: The dimension formula for the centralizer
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identity relating the degrees of the algebra and of its commutant, from which the degree of the chosen algebra is computed.

core_obligations: The second condition implies the first (proof lines 863-874): assuming an algebra similar to the given one, of the prescribed degree and containing the splitting field, it suffices to show that its scalar extension to that field is a matrix algebra; using that the tensor product with the opposite algebra is an endomorphism algebra and that the field is its own centralizer there, the extension is identified with the endomorphisms of the algebra as a vector space over the field.

The first condition implies the second (proof lines 876-892): assuming the algebra splits over the field, one fixes an isomorphism with an endomorphism algebra, takes as candidate the commutant of the algebra inside the endomorphisms of the ambient vector space, notes that the field sits inside it, and uses the stated lemmas to see that its class is the negative of the given class; the dimension formula then computes its degree and shows it equals the square of the degree of the field, after which the observation that the field splits the class exactly when it splits the opposite class closes the argument.
proof_roadmap: For the first direction, identify the scalar extension with an endomorphism algebra using self centralizing subfields.
For the converse, take the commutant of the algebra inside an endomorphism algebra.
Use the Brauer group relation and the dimension formula to get similarity and the correct degree, then pass to the opposite class.
difficulty_reason: The theorem characterizes when a finite field extension splits a finite central simple algebra, namely exactly when some algebra similar to the given one contains the field as a subfield of the maximum possible dimension (statement lines 851-861). The proof is a complete argument: the easier direction identifies the scalar extension of the similar algebra with an endomorphism algebra using a named result on self centralizing subfields (proof lines 863-874); the converse takes the commutant of the algebra inside an endomorphism algebra and uses the Brauer group relation to see that it is similar to the given algebra, then computes its degree by the dimension formula for centralizers and passes to the opposite class (proof lines 876-892). The non-formal content is the identification of the centralizer with the endomorphism algebra and the final dimension count. The claim is H2.
